# Data samples: news-and-markets

Every data type of `news-and-markets` as a real record of the committed test data, every field explained from its data contract, the fields only other rows have and a checklist for the production query. The [index](README.md) lists every domain.

<a id="quote"></a>

## Quote and price history: quote (QUOTE)

A quote and recent price history for a ticker, as the yfinance connector computed them. One row per quote and price history, keyed by QUOTE_ID. Read by the **news-and-markets** pack's connector `news-store`. A **snapshot of public data**, captured 2026-10-18T03:24:33Z from Yahoo Finance (yfinance connector), refreshed whole by its script (External data); 20 records. A refresh replaces the whole snapshot.

### File layout

|  |  |
|---|---|
| Path | `data/testdata/news-and-markets/quote/` + `quote.YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl.gz` |
| Format | JSON Lines: UTF-8, one JSON object a line, gzip-compressed (`.jsonl.gz`) |
| Key field | `QUOTE_ID` |
| Date field | none in the record: a snapshot of public data, its file named by the capture date; the demo lake serves the same records on every business date (partition `business_date`) |
| Promoted columns | none (the whole record is kept as `doc`) |
| Vector fields | none |
| Partitioned by | `business_date` |
| A day's file | the whole snapshot |

### Field reference

Every field of the record above, nested ones as dotted paths (`[]` marks an array of objects). *Required* is the contract's; *in N%* is how often the test data fills it.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning | Values, format, unit | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `QUOTE_ID` | string | required | The record's id (the business key) | pattern `^QUOTE-`; links to `quote` | `"QUOTE-AAPL"` |
| `SYMBOL` | string | required | The Yahoo Finance symbol quoted (chart meta symbol). | — | `"AAPL"` |
| `NAME` | string | required | The instrument's name (Yahoo's long name, else its short name). | — | `"Apple Inc."` |
| `EXCHANGE` | string | required | The exchange's name as Yahoo gives it (chart meta fullExchangeName, else exchangeName): NasdaqGS, NYSE. | one of `NYSE`, `NasdaqGS` | `"NasdaqGS"` |
| `CURRENCY` | string | required | The currency of every price of the quote, ISO 4217 (Yahoo chart meta currency). | — | `"USD"` |
| `INSTRUMENT_TYPE` | string | required | Yahoo's instrument type (EQUITY, ETF, INDEX...). | — | `"EQUITY"` |
| `PRICE` | number | required | The last traded price (Yahoo chart meta regularMarketPrice, else the last bar's close). | unit: currency units of CURRENCY | `343.46` |
| `PREVIOUS_CLOSE` | number | required | The previous session's closing price (Yahoo chart meta). | unit: currency units of CURRENCY | `342.0` |
| `CHANGE` | number | required | PRICE minus PREVIOUS_CLOSE, gain positive. | unit: currency units of CURRENCY | `1.4599999999999795` |
| `CHANGE_PCT` | number | required | CHANGE as a percentage of PREVIOUS_CLOSE, in percent (0.43 is 0.43%), gain positive. | unit: percent | `0.4269005847953157` |
| `DAY_LOW` | number | required | The session's lowest price. | unit: currency units of CURRENCY | `340.46` |
| `DAY_HIGH` | number | required | The session's highest price. | unit: currency units of CURRENCY | `347.82` |
| `FIFTY_TWO_WEEK_LOW` | number | required | The lowest price over the last 52 weeks (Yahoo fiftyTwoWeekLow). | unit: currency units of CURRENCY | `243.42` |
| `FIFTY_TWO_WEEK_HIGH` | number | required | The highest price over the last 52 weeks (Yahoo fiftyTwoWeekHigh). | unit: currency units of CURRENCY | `348.15` |
| `VOLUME` | number | required | The session's traded volume (Yahoo regularMarketVolume). | unit: shares | `59852690.0` |
| `MARKET_STATE` | string | required | The market's state when fetched: Yahoo's marketState as given, else REGULAR or CLOSED from the regular trading period, else UNKNOWN. | — | `"CLOSED"` |
| `AS_OF` | string | required | When the quoted price was last traded, as text: local time and the exchange's time zone; in the snapshot it ends with "(snapshot captured <date>)". | seen: `2026-10-16 16:00 America/New_York (snapshot captured 2026-10-18)`, `2026-10-16 16:03 America/New_York (snapshot captured 2026-10-18)`, `2026-10-16 16:02 America/New_York (snapshot captured 2026-10-18)` | `"2026-10-16 16:00 America/New_York (snapshot captured 2026-…` |
| `HISTORY` | array of objects | required | The daily bars of the last year, oldest first, one element per trading day: DATE, OPEN, HIGH, LOW, CLOSE and VOLUME. | — | [251 objects] |
| `HISTORY[].DATE` | date (YYYY-MM-DD) | required | The bar's date (YYYY-MM-DD for daily bars). | — | `"2025-10-17"` |
| `HISTORY[].OPEN` | number | required | The bar's opening price. | unit: currency units of CURRENCY | `248.02000427246094` |
| `HISTORY[].HIGH` | number | required | The bar's highest price. | unit: currency units of CURRENCY | `253.3800048828125` |
| `HISTORY[].LOW` | number | required | The bar's lowest price. | unit: currency units of CURRENCY | `247.27000427246094` |
| `HISTORY[].CLOSE` | number | required | The bar's closing price. | unit: currency units of CURRENCY | `252.2899932861328` |
| `HISTORY[].VOLUME` | number | required | The bar's traded volume. | unit: shares | `49147000.0` |
| `DAY_RANGE` | string | required | DAY_LOW – DAY_HIGH as text. | — | `"340.46 – 347.82"` |
| `FIFTY_TWO_WEEK_RANGE` | string | required | FIFTY_TWO_WEEK_LOW – FIFTY_TWO_WEEK_HIGH as text. | — | `"243.42 – 348.15"` |
| `HISTORY_RANGE` | string | required | The span of HISTORY asked of Yahoo (the connector's range setting, 1y). | — | `"1y"` |
| `INTERVAL` | string | required | The spacing of HISTORY's bars (the connector's interval setting, 1d). | — | `"1d"` |
| `PROVENANCE` | object | required | Where the quote comes from, one object: FEED (Yahoo Finance's public chart endpoint), FETCHED (ISO-8601 UTC), CACHED_FOR, TERMS and SNAPSHOT. | — | {…} |
| `PROVENANCE.FEED` | string | required | The feed the quote came from (Yahoo Finance's public chart endpoint). | — | `"Yahoo Finance public chart endpoint (unofficial)"` |
| `PROVENANCE.FETCHED` | timestamp (ISO-8601) | required | When the connector fetched the quote, ISO-8601 UTC. | — | `"2026-10-18T03:24:33.511628799Z"` |
| `PROVENANCE.CACHED_FOR` | string | required | How long the connector caches a fetch (its cache TTL), as text. | — | `"3600 s"` |
| `PROVENANCE.TERMS` | string | required | The terms the data may be used under. | — | `"Sample and internal demonstration use only; not for produc…` |
| `PROVENANCE.SNAPSHOT` | string | required | Says the document is served from the committed snapshot in the demo lake, not live, and that the data belongs to its providers. | — | `"Snapshot captured 2026-10-18 03:24 UTC from Yahoo Finance;…` |
| `SNAPSHOT` | string | required | Says the document is a committed snapshot: when it was captured and from where (tools/testdata/capture_market.py). | — | `"Snapshot captured 2026-10-18 03:24 UTC from Yahoo Finance"` |
| `SNAPSHOT_CAPTURED_AT` | timestamp (ISO-8601) | required | When the snapshot was captured, ISO-8601 UTC. | — | `"2026-10-18T03:24:33Z"` |

### For the production query

- **Identity:** one record per `QUOTE_ID` per `snapshot`; the key is text, unique within the date.
- **Never null:** `QUOTE_ID`, `SYMBOL`, `NAME`, `EXCHANGE`, `CURRENCY`, `INSTRUMENT_TYPE`, `PRICE`, `PREVIOUS_CLOSE`, `CHANGE`, `CHANGE_PCT`, `DAY_LOW`, `DAY_HIGH`, `FIFTY_TWO_WEEK_LOW`, `FIFTY_TWO_WEEK_HIGH`, `VOLUME`, `MARKET_STATE`, `AS_OF`, `HISTORY`, `DAY_RANGE`, `FIFTY_TWO_WEEK_RANGE`, `HISTORY_RANGE`, `INTERVAL`, `PROVENANCE`, `SNAPSHOT`, `SNAPSHOT_CAPTURED_AT` (the contract's required fields).
- **Format:** JSON Lines, UTF-8, one object a line, gzip; field names exactly as shown (UPPER_SNAKE); dates `YYYY-MM-DD`; numbers as JSON numbers, never strings; a missing value is `null` or absent (an empty string is read as empty).
- **Arrays:** keep the order shown (vectors in the scenario set's or the run's order); nested objects as JSON, never flattened.
- Unique: `QUOTE_ID` per snapshot.
- `QUOTE_ID` matches `^QUOTE-`.

## Headlines: news (NEWS)

The headlines for one name, as the news connector computed them: newest first, filtered for relevance, duplicates removed. One row per headlines, keyed by NEWS_ID. Read by the **news-and-markets** pack's connector `news-store`. A **snapshot of public data**, captured 2026-10-18T03:24:33Z from Google News (news connector), refreshed whole by its script (External data); 71 records. A refresh replaces the whole snapshot.

### File layout

|  |  |
|---|---|
| Path | `data/testdata/news-and-markets/news/` + `news.YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl.gz` |
| Format | JSON Lines: UTF-8, one JSON object a line, gzip-compressed (`.jsonl.gz`) |
| Key field | `NEWS_ID` |
| Date field | none in the record: a snapshot of public data, its file named by the capture date; the demo lake serves the same records on every business date (partition `business_date`) |
| Promoted columns | none (the whole record is kept as `doc`) |
| Vector fields | none |
| Partitioned by | `business_date` |
| A day's file | the whole snapshot |

### Field reference

Every field of the record above, nested ones as dotted paths (`[]` marks an array of objects). *Required* is the contract's; *in N%* is how often the test data fills it.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning | Values, format, unit | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `NEWS_ID` | string | required | The record's id (the business key) | pattern `^NEWS-`; links to `news` | `"NEWS-Alphabet"` |
| `ENTITY` | string | required | The company or topic the headlines are about, as searched (Alphabet, Federal Reserve). | — | `"Alphabet"` |
| `ALIASES` | array of strings | required | Other names of the entity; a headline must name the entity or one of these to pass the relevance step. | — | [2 values] |
| `EDITION` | string | required | The Google News edition the headlines come from: language and country (en-US, de-DE, ja-JP). | one of `de-DE`, `en-US`, `ja-JP` | `"en-US"` |
| `RELEVANCE_FILTER` | string | required | on when headlines not about ENTITY were dropped (the pipeline's relevance step), off for the ~all record. | one of `off`, `on` | `"on"` |
| `COUNT` | integer | required | How many headlines ITEMS holds: at most the news connector's max-items setting (15 in the snapshot). | — | `15` |
| `FETCHED_AT` | string | required | When the headlines were fetched, as text: date and time in UTC, and in the snapshot "(snapshot captured <date>)". | one of `2026-10-18 03:25 UTC (snapshot captured 2026-10-18)`, `2026-10-18 03:26 UTC (snapshot captured 2026-10-18)`, `2026-10-18 03:27 UTC (snapshot captured 2026-10-18)` | `"2026-10-18 03:25 UTC (snapshot captured 2026-10-18)"` |
| `ITEMS` | array of objects | required | The headlines, newest first, one element each: PUBLISHED, SOURCE (the publisher), TITLE and LINK. | — | [15 objects] |
| `ITEMS[].PUBLISHED` | string | required | When the headline was published, as text (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC). | — | `"2026-10-18 01:37 UTC"` |
| `ITEMS[].SOURCE` | string | required | The publisher of the headline. | — | `"Simply Wall Street"` |
| `ITEMS[].TITLE` | string | required | The headline as the publisher wrote it. | — | `"Alphabet (GOOGL) Plans Toronto Robotaxi Service By 2028"` |
| `ITEMS[].LINK` | string | required | The link to the article (a Google News redirect URL). | — | `"https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiugFBVV95cUxOWF9ZU…` |
| `BY_SOURCE` | array of objects | required | How many of the headlines each publisher wrote, one element per publisher: SOURCE and COUNT. | — | [12 objects] |
| `BY_SOURCE[].SOURCE` | string | required | A publisher among ITEMS. | — | `"The Motley Fool"` |
| `BY_SOURCE[].COUNT` | integer | required | How many of ITEMS that publisher has. | — | `3` |
| `PIPELINE` | array of objects | required | What each step of the news pipeline did, one element per step in order (relevance, duplicates …): STEP, KEPT and DROPPED (headline counts). | — | [3 objects] |
| `PIPELINE[].DROPPED` | integer | required | How many headlines the step removed. | — | `4` |
| `PIPELINE[].KEPT` | integer | required | How many headlines remained after the step. | — | `96` |
| `PIPELINE[].STEP` | string | required | The pipeline step, in order: relevance (the title names the entity or an alias), duplicates (the same story or headline from the same publisher kept once, the newest), limit (at most the connector's max-items); sources (deny or allow lists) when set. | one of `duplicates`, `limit`, `relevance` | `"relevance"` |
| `FETCHED` | integer | required | How many headlines the feed returned before the pipeline (relevance, duplicates, limit) filtered them. | seen: `100`, `102`, `104`, `101`, `103`, `106`, `92` | `100` |
| `PROVENANCE` | object | required | Where the headlines come from, one object: FEED (Google News RSS), FETCHED, CACHED_FOR, TERMS and SNAPSHOT. | — | {…} |
| `PROVENANCE.FEED` | string | required | The feed the headlines came from (Google News RSS). | — | `"Google News RSS (news.google.com)"` |
| `PROVENANCE.FETCHED` | string | required | When the connector fetched the feed, as text (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC). | one of `2026-10-18 03:25 UTC`, `2026-10-18 03:26 UTC`, `2026-10-18 03:27 UTC` | `"2026-10-18 03:25 UTC"` |
| `PROVENANCE.CACHED_FOR` | string | required | How long the connector caches a fetch (its cache TTL), as text. | — | `"3600 s"` |
| `PROVENANCE.TERMS` | string | required | The terms the headlines may be shown under. | — | `"Headlines and links belong to their publishers; shown for …` |
| `PROVENANCE.SNAPSHOT` | string | required | Says the document is served from the committed snapshot in the demo lake, not live. | — | `"Snapshot captured 2026-10-18 03:24 UTC from Google News; s…` |
| `SNAPSHOT` | string | required | Says the document is a committed snapshot: when it was captured and from where (tools/testdata/capture_market.py). | — | `"Snapshot captured 2026-10-18 03:24 UTC from Google News"` |
| `SNAPSHOT_CAPTURED_AT` | timestamp (ISO-8601) | required | When the snapshot was captured, ISO-8601 UTC. | — | `"2026-10-18T03:24:33Z"` |

### For the production query

- **Identity:** one record per `NEWS_ID` per `snapshot`; the key is text, unique within the date.
- **Never null:** `NEWS_ID`, `ENTITY`, `ALIASES`, `EDITION`, `RELEVANCE_FILTER`, `COUNT`, `FETCHED_AT`, `ITEMS`, `BY_SOURCE`, `PIPELINE`, `FETCHED`, `PROVENANCE`, `SNAPSHOT`, `SNAPSHOT_CAPTURED_AT` (the contract's required fields).
- **Format:** JSON Lines, UTF-8, one object a line, gzip; field names exactly as shown (UPPER_SNAKE); dates `YYYY-MM-DD`; numbers as JSON numbers, never strings; a missing value is `null` or absent (an empty string is read as empty).
- **Arrays:** keep the order shown (vectors in the scenario set's or the run's order); nested objects as JSON, never flattened.
- Unique: `NEWS_ID` per snapshot.
- `NEWS_ID` matches `^NEWS-`.
- `COUNT` is at least 0.
- `BY_SOURCE[].COUNT` is at least 0.

<a id="news-topic"></a>

## News topic: news-topic (TOPIC)

A topic and the news about it: headlines (newest first) with their publishers and links, a count by source, and how the headlines were chosen. One row per news topic, keyed by TOPIC_ID. Read by the **news-and-markets** pack's connector `news-store` (lake table `news.news-topic`). There is **no committed test data** for this kind: the sample comes from the pack's samples (`config/packs/economy/news-and-markets/samples/news-topic.jsonl`, 15 records). A bank or a public refresh delivers it in the same JSON Lines shape.

### File layout

|  |  |
|---|---|
| Path | `config/packs/economy/news-and-markets/samples/news-topic.jsonl` |
| Format | JSON Lines: UTF-8, one JSON object a line |
| Key field | `TOPIC_ID` |
| Date field | none in the record: the pack's samples are served on every business date (partition `business_date`) |
| Promoted columns | none (the whole record is kept as `doc`) |
| Vector fields | none |
| Partitioned by | `business_date` |
| A day's file | no committed files |

### One sample record

A real record, the most complete of the 15 (the one with the most non-empty fields), pretty-printed with two-space indents. **A string such as `"… 506 more numbers"` inside an array marks a fold**: it stands for the elements left out and is not part of the data.

### Field reference

Every field of the record above, nested ones as dotted paths (`[]` marks an array of objects). *Required* is the contract's; *in N%* is how often the test data fills it.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning | Values, format, unit | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TOPIC_ID` | string | required | The record's id (the business key) | pattern `^TOPIC-` | `"TOPIC-INDIA"` |
| `NAME` | string | required | The topic's name as searched (Federal Reserve, Bank of Japan). | — | `"India"` |
| `CATEGORY` | string | required | What the topic is: Central bank, Theme, Country or Company. | one of `Central bank`, `Company`, `Country`, `Theme` | `"Country"` |
| `ALIASES` | array of strings | required | Other names of the topic the news connector accepts in a headline (its relevance step). | — | [2 values] |
| `ALIAS_TEXT` | string | required | Other names the headlines may use for the topic, comma-separated ("Fed, FOMC, Powell"). | — | `"Indian, New Delhi"` |
| `EDITION` | string | required | The Google News edition searched (en-US, de-DE, ja-JP), or default for the connector's own. | seen: `default`, `de-DE`, `ja-JP` | `"default"` |
| `NEWS_ID` | string | required | The topic's headlines with the relevance filter on: a NEWS_ID of the news kind (NEWS-<name>). | pattern `^NEWS-`; links to `news` | `"NEWS-India"` |
| `NEWS_ALL_ID` | string | required | The topic's headlines without the relevance filter: a NEWS_ID of the news kind (NEWS-<name>~all). | pattern `^NEWS-`; links to `news` | `"NEWS-India~all"` |
| `ECONOMY` | string | optional (filled in 33% of rows) | The economy the topic belongs to: an id of the world-economy pack's economy kind (ECON-<ISO 3166-1 alpha-3>). | pattern `^ECON-`; links to `economy` | `"ECON-IND"` |
| `_meta` | object | optional (filled in every row) | The generator's provenance stamp, one object; optional, carried through in the stored document and not read by Drishti (the contracts leave it out). A bank's extract may omit it. | — | {…} |
| `_meta.source` | string | optional (filled in every `_meta` entry) | The source system or public source the record was built from (sec-edgar, gleif, …). | — | `"reference"` |
| `_meta.generation` | integer | optional (filled in every `_meta` entry) | The generator's format generation (always 1). | — | `1` |
| `_meta.live` | boolean | optional (filled in every `_meta` entry) | Part of the generator's provenance stamp; carried through, not read by Drishti. | — | `false` |

### For the production query

- **Identity:** one record per `TOPIC_ID` per `snapshot`; the key is text, unique within the date.

- **Format:** JSON Lines, UTF-8, one object a line, gzip; field names exactly as shown (UPPER_SNAKE); dates `YYYY-MM-DD`; numbers as JSON numbers, never strings; a missing value is `null` or absent (an empty string is read as empty).

<a id="listed-company"></a>

## Listed company: listed-company (CO)

A listed company: its live quote and price history (yfinance connector) and its news headlines (news connector), both computed on demand. One row per listed company, keyed by COMPANY_ID. Read by the **news-and-markets** pack's connector `news-store` (lake table `news.listed-company`). There is **no committed test data** for this kind: the sample comes from the pack's samples (`config/packs/economy/news-and-markets/samples/listed-company.jsonl`, 20 records). A bank or a public refresh delivers it in the same JSON Lines shape.

### File layout

|  |  |
|---|---|
| Path | `config/packs/economy/news-and-markets/samples/listed-company.jsonl` |
| Format | JSON Lines: UTF-8, one JSON object a line |
| Key field | `COMPANY_ID` |
| Date field | none in the record: the pack's samples are served on every business date (partition `business_date`) |
| Promoted columns | none (the whole record is kept as `doc`) |
| Vector fields | none |
| Partitioned by | `business_date` |
| A day's file | no committed files |

### One sample record

A real record, the most complete of the 20 (the one with the most non-empty fields), pretty-printed with two-space indents. **A string such as `"… 506 more numbers"` inside an array marks a fold**: it stands for the elements left out and is not part of the data.

```json
{
  "COMPANY_ID": "CO-AAPL",
  "TICKER": "AAPL",
  "NAME": "Apple Inc.",
  "ALIASES": [
    "Apple Inc",
    "AAPL",
    "iPhone"
  ],
  "ALIAS_TEXT": "Apple Inc, AAPL, iPhone",
  "EXCHANGE": "Nasdaq",
  "SECTOR": "Technology",
  "COUNTRY": "US",
  "ECONOMY": "ECON-USA",
  "QUOTE_ID": "QUOTE-AAPL",
  "NEWS_ID": "NEWS-Apple",
  "NEWS_ALL_ID": "NEWS-Apple~all",
  "_meta": {
    "source": "reference",
    "generation": 1,
    "live": false
  }
}
```

### Field reference

Every field of the record above, nested ones as dotted paths (`[]` marks an array of objects). *Required* is the contract's; *in N%* is how often the test data fills it.
